From Middle Persian bʾl (bār, “load, burden; duty; fruit”), from Proto-Iranian *bāra- (“load”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰer- (“to bear, carry”).
From Middle Persian bʾl (bār, “time, occasion”).

Inherited from Middle Persian wʾčʾl (wāzār, “market”); see it for further information.

parole.significato: to withhold, to restrain, to prevent
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (LAWHL-dʾštn' /⁠abāz dāštan⁠/, “to withhold, restrain, prevent”). By surface analysis, باز (bāz /bâz, “again”) + داشتن (dāštan /dâštan, “to keep”).
From earlier بازارگان (bâzârgân), from Middle Persian wʾčʾlkʾn' (wāzāragān, “merchant”). Compare Old Armenian վաճառական (vačaṙakan). Analyzable as بازار (bâzâr, “bazaar”) + ـگان (gân).
Inherited from Middle Persian 𐭡𐭠𐭮𐭲𐭠𐭭 (bʾstʾn /⁠bāstān⁠/).

From Middle Persian, also borrowed from Arabic بَاشَق (bāšaq). Akin to Mazanderani واشه (wāša, “sparrowhawk”) and Northern Kurdish waşe (“sparrow-hawk”). Connected to Sanskrit भास (bhāsa, “a bird of prey”) and to Persian باز (bāz, “falcon, hawk”).
Inherited from Middle Persian bʾg, from Old Persian *bāgah, from Proto-Iranian *bāgáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *bʰāgás, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂g-ó-s, from *bʰeh₂g- + *-ós.

From Middle Persian [script needed] (wp- /⁠waf-⁠/, “to weave”), from Proto-Iranian *wabdi, Proto-Indo-Iranian *wabdʰi, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *webʰ-. Compare Greek υφαίνω (yfaíno), English weave, Avestan ubdaēna ("made of cloth"), and Sanskrit उभ्नाति (ubhnāti, “entwine”).
From Middle Persian b’lk’ (bālag, “wing”), Northern Luri بال (bal, “arm, wing”).

Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (bʾlyn' /⁠balēn⁠/, “cushion; pillow”).

From Middle Persian 𐭥𐭠𐭭𐭢 (ʿʾng /⁠vāng⁠/), probably from Proto-Indo-European *wṓkʷs (“voice, speech”). Akin to Old Armenian վանգ (vang), an Iranian borrowing.

From Middle Persian wlcykl (/⁠warzīgar⁠/, “peasant”). By surface analysis, برز (“sown field; seed; agriculture”) + ـگَر (“-er”).

Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (th /⁠tah⁠/), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *tews- (“to be empty, drain”), and thus cognate with تهی (tohi, “empty, hollow”), Sanskrit तुच्छ्य (tucchya, “empty, vain”). Compare also Persian تک (tak, “bottom”).

From Middle Persian twhyg (tuhīg, “empty; vain, illusory; barren”), from Proto-Iranian *tuŝyás, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *tuŝćyás, from Proto-Indo-European *tus-sḱ-yós, from *tews- (“to be empty”). Cognate with Vedic Sanskrit तुच्छ्य (tucchyá).

From Middle Persian 𐭫𐭪 (LK /⁠tō⁠/, “you, thou”), from Old Persian (compare 𐎬𐎺𐎶 (tuvam)), from Proto-Iranian *tuHám (compare Northern Kurdish tu, Pashto ته (tə), Avestan 𐬙𐬏𐬨 (tūm)), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *tuHám, from Proto-Indo-European *túh₂.

Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (twbʾn' /⁠tuwān⁠/, “might; power”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *tewh₂- (“to swell, grow, become strong”). Compare Sanskrit तवस् (tavas, “force, power”), Avestan 𐬙𐬎𐬙𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬀 (tutauua, “to be able”), Proto-Slavic *tỳti (“to become fat”), Ancient Greek

From Middle Persian *tōbrag (“bag, sack”), cognate with Sanskrit टोपर (ṭopara, “a small bag”). Compare Middle Armenian տոպրակ (toprak, “sack”), Arabic طَرْبُوق (ṭarbūq, “legging”), Classical Syriac ܛܽܘܒܪܰܩܐ (ṭūḇarqā, “nosebag of an ass”), Middle Iranian borrowings. See also Classical Persian تَرْبو
From Middle Persian, borrowed into Arabic تُوذَرِيج (tūḏarīj), Classical Syriac ܛܘܕܪܝܓ (ṭudrīg). An unsuffixed form appears in تُوذَر (tūḏar) and ܬܘܕܪܐ (tudrā).

parole.significato: provisions (food that you take on a trip)
parole.testo: From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (twšk' /⁠tōšag⁠/, “provisions”). Compare Old Armenian թոշակ (tʻošak), an Iranian borrowing.

Inherited from Middle Persian twlkʾ (/⁠tōlag⁠/, “baby animal, whelp”), from Avestan 𐬙𐬀𐬎𐬭𐬎𐬥𐬀 (taᵘruna, “young”), Northern Luri تیله (tilə). Cognate with Sanskrit तरुण (taruṇa, “juvenile”). Cf. تور (tōr /tur, “uncivilized”).
Inherited from Middle Persian *tōlag, whence also Arabic طَوْلَق (ṭawlaq, “mallow”). Probably a variation of ترشه (turša /torše, “sorrel, dock”), تور (tōr /tur, “rosy dock”)
Probably cognate with Persian توه (tuh, “layer”), from Middle Persian [script needed] (twp /⁠*tōf⁠/, “layer”).

From Middle Persian tk' (tag, “running; attack”), from Proto-Indo-European *tekʷ-. Related to تاختن (tâxtan, “to attack”), and also related to Old Armenian ասպատակ (aspatak); which is an Iranian borrowing.
From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (tkwk' /⁠takōk⁠/, “drinking vessel”). Compare Old Armenian թակոյկ (tʻakoyk) and Old Georgian ტაკუკი (ṭaḳuḳi).
From Middle Persian tklg (tagarg, “hail”). Akin to Manichaean Middle Persian tgrg (tagarg), Northern Luri تیرد (teyerd).

From Middle Persian 𐭧𐭲𐭩𐭠 (ḥtyʾ), [Book Pahlavi needed] (HTYA), [Book Pahlavi needed] (tgl), 𐫤𐫏𐫃𐫡 (tygr /⁠tigr, tīr⁠/, “arrow”), from Old Persian [Term?], compare 𐎫𐎡𐎥𐎼 (t-i-g-r /⁠tigraʰ⁠/, “sharp”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬙𐬌𐬖𐬭𐬌 (tiγri, “arrow”), 𐬙𐬌𐬖𐬭𐬀 (tiγra, “sharp”).
Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (tylk' /⁠tērag⁠/, “dark”).

Inherited from Middle Persian gyʾg (gyāg, “place”), from Proto-Iranian *wi-Hwah-, from *wi- + *Hwah- (“to dwell”).
From جا (jâ) + بیز (biz), the second element may derive from Middle Persian wyhyc- (/⁠wihēz-⁠/, “to move, progress”), or Middle Persian wyc- (/⁠wēz-⁠/, “to swing, throw”).
Inherited from Middle Persian 𐭩𐭠𐭲𐭥𐭪𐭠 (yʾtʿkʾ /⁠ǰādūg⁠/, “wizardry; wizard”), from Old Persian 𐎹𐎠𐎬𐎢 (y-a-tu-u /⁠yātu⁠/), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *yaHtúš. Cognate with Sanskrit या॒तु (yātú).

Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gywʼk'-rōb /⁠gyāg-rōb⁠/, “broom”). By surface analysis, جا (jâ, “place”) + روب (rub, present stem of روبیدن (rubidan, “to sweep”)). Unrelated to Hindi झाड़ू (jhāṛū) / Urdu جھاڑُو (jhāṛū).
From Middle Persian [script needed] (ǰām, “glass”). Related to Avestan 𐬫𐬀𐬨𐬀 (yama, “glass”).

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (ywmb-ytn' /⁠jumbīdan⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *Hyámbdi (“to move around”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃yebʰ- (“to enter into”).

From Middle Persian thorn (hʾl /⁠xār⁠/), related to Sanskrit खर (khara, “sharp, rough, harsh”)). Compare Manichaean Middle Persian xʾr (xār).

From Middle Persian gryhcg (grehčag, “pit, prison”). Akin to Parthian [Term?] (“pit”); and related to Middle Persian [script needed] (gristag, “cave, enclosure”).
From Middle Persian [script needed] (gc /⁠gaz⁠/, “tamarisk”). Compare Old Armenian գազ (gaz, “milkvetch”), an Iranian borrowing.
From Middle Persian [script needed] (gt' /⁠gad⁠/, “rod, club”), from Proto-Iranian *gádaH, Proto-Indo-Iranian *gadaH (“club”).

parole.significato: to express, to announce, to explain
parole.testo: From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (wcʾltn' /⁠wizārdan, wizār-⁠/, “to separate; to explain, interpret; to perform, fulfil, redeem”), from Proto-Iranian *wí (“apart”) + a causative formation from Proto-Iranian *čarH (“to come and go, wander”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wí + Proto-Indo-Iranian *

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (wyz'stn', wyz'd- /⁠wizāstan, wizāy-⁠/, “to injure, impair; prejudice”), of which only the present stem infinitive made it to New Persian. Not at all related to گزیدن (gazîdan).

Inherited from Middle Persian *gazar. Compare Sanskrit गार्जर (gārjara), Classical Syriac ܓܙܪܐ (gezzārāʾ), Hebrew גֶּזֶר (gézer), Pashto ګازره (gāzara), Alviri-Vidari گزر (gazer), Baluchi گزرک (gizirk, gazirk), Kurdish gêzer, گێزەر (gêzer), Northern Luri گزر (gezer). Compare also the Turkic borrowin
Inherited from Middle Persian wsydy (/⁠wizend⁠/, “hurt, harm, injury”), a prefixed form of Proto-Iranian *ǰán-. See زَدَن (zadan) for more.

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gzytn' /⁠gazīdan⁠/). Cognate with Gilaki گشتن (gaštən) (present stem: گز (gaz)), Central Kurdish گەستن (gestin) and Northern Kurdish gestin. Compare Old Armenian գազան (gazan), an Iranian borrowing.

From Middle Persian [Term?] (/⁠wizīdan⁠/), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kʷey- (“to pay”). Compare Baluchi گچین (gechén, “choice”), Northern Kurdish bijartin and Old Armenian վճիտ (včit), an Iranian borrowing.
From Middle Persian wstʾhw' (wistāx, “confident, bold”), from wistāxw, from Old Persian *vistāhuva-. Akin to Old Armenian վստահ (vstah), an Iranian borrowing.

Inherited from Middle Persian wstltn' (/⁠wistardan⁠/), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *str̥náHti, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *sterh₃-. Compare Avestan 𐬯𐬙𐬀𐬭- (star-, “to spread”)), Latin sternō (“to bestrew, sprinkle”), Sanskrit स्तृणाति (stṛṇā́ti), Ancient Greek στόρνῡμι (stórnūmi), Old Church Sla

parole.significato: to split; to take apart; to disconnect
parole.testo: From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (wsstn' /⁠wisistan⁠/, “to break, split”), from Proto-Iranian *wi- + *said-, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *skeyd- (Cheung 2007). Cognate with Baluchi سندگ (sendag, “to break, split”), Latin scindo, and Ancient Greek σχίζω (skhízō).

From Middle Persian 𐮅𐮍𐮎𐮈 (wspy), from Old Persian 𐎻𐎿𐎱 (vi-s-p /⁠vispa⁠/), a borrowing from Old Median [Term?] (/⁠*vispa⁠/). Inherited from Proto-Iranian *wícwah (“all, every; whole”), Proto-Indo-Iranian *wíćwas (“all, every”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(h₁)wiḱ/wo-. Perhaps influenced from
From Middle Persian [script needed] (wšwp-tn' /⁠wišuftan⁠/, “to disturb, destroy”).

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gšnyc /⁠gišnīz⁠/, “coriander”). Cognate with Central Kurdish گژنیژ (gijnîj), Baluchi [script needed] (gēnīč). Compare the Iranian borrowings: Old Armenian գինձ (ginj), Old Georgian ქინძი (kinʒi), Mandarin 胡荽 (húsuī).

Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (wšʾtn' /⁠wišādan⁠/, “to open, loose, free”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *sh₂ey- (“to bind, fetter”) with the preverb *wi-. "To conquer": semantic loan from Arabic فَتَحَ (fataḥa, “to open; to conquer”).

Inherited from Middle Persian gwptn', from Old Persian 𐎥𐎢𐎲𐎫𐎡𐎹 (g-u-b-t-i-y /⁠gaubataiy⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *gáwbati. Cognate with Russian говорить (govoritʹ) and Old Church Slavonic говорити (govoriti).
Inherited from Late Middle Persian gwl (gul, “rose, flower”), from Old Persian *vr̥dah, ultimately inherited from Proto-Iranian *wardah, *wr̥dah.
Inherited from Middle Persian TYNA / gl (gil).
From Middle Persian [script needed] (g(y)lk’ /⁠gilag⁠/, “complaint, lamentation”). Compare Baluchi گِلَگ (gilag, “complaint”).
Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (glwk' /⁠galōg⁠/), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷel- (“throat”). Cognate with Latin gula (“throat”) and Sanskrit गल (gala, “throat, neck”).

parole.significato: to appoint, to consign to (someone to a post or role)
parole.testo: From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gwmʾl-tn' /⁠gumārdan⁠/), 𐫃𐫇𐫖𐫀𐫡𐫅𐫗 (gwmʾrdn /⁠gumārdan⁠/, “to appoint, commission, entrust”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *mere (“to delay, hinder”). Cognate with Latin mora (“delay”).

Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (gwmʾn' /⁠gumān⁠/, “doubt”), from Proto-Iranian *wimānah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian. Compare Avestan 𐬬𐬍𐬨𐬀𐬥𐬋 (vīmanō, one of the Ahrimanic plagues: doubt?), Sanskrit विमनस् (vimanas, “sad, disconsolate”) Northern Luri گمو (gemo).

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (wnʾs /⁠wināh⁠/), 𐫇𐫏𐫗𐫀𐫍 (wynʾh /⁠wināh⁠/, “sin, crime”), ultimately from the Proto-Iranian preverb *vi- (from Proto-Indo-European *wí (“apart, against”)) and the root *nas- (“to disappear; to perish”), from Proto-Indo-European *neḱ- (“to perish, to disappear
Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (wnʾskʾl /⁠wināhgār⁠/). Equivalent to گناه (gonâh) + ـکار (-kâr).

Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (gwmbt' /⁠gumbad⁠/, “dome, fire-temple”), from Classical Syriac ܩܘܒܬܐ (qubbəṯā). Doublet of قبه (qobbe, “dome”), also from Syriac but through Arabic. Compare Old Armenian գմբեթ (gmbetʻ) and Georgian გუმბათი (gumbati), Iranian borrowings.
From Middle Persian [Term?] (/⁠ganǰ⁠/, “treasure”), from Old Persian *ganzah (“treasure”), probably from Old Median *ganǰam (“treasure”). See Arabic كَنْز (kanz, “treasure”).
From Middle Persian wncšk' (winjišk), from earlier *winǰaičakah. Compare Baluchi جنجشک (jinjišk), Southwestern Fars بجشک (beješk), بیجیشک (bijišk).

From earlier گنجوَر (ganjwar) and گنجَر (ganjar), from Middle Persian 𐭢𐭭𐭦𐭥𐭡𐭥 (gncwbl /⁠ganjwar⁠/) (Manichaean Middle Persian 𐫃𐫗𐫉𐫇𐫡 (gnzwr /⁠ganzwar⁠/)), from Old Persian *ganzabarah, from Old Median *ganǰabarah. Equivalent to گنج (ganj, “treasure”) + ـور (-war /-var) or +ـر (-ur/-ar) .
From Middle Persian gwnd (/⁠gund⁠/).

From Middle Persian 𐫃𐫗𐫇𐫖 (gnwm /⁠gannum⁠/), (in book Pahlavi 𐭤𐭢 (Hᵍ /⁠gan(d)um⁠/)) from Proto-Iranian, from Proto-Indo-Iranian. Compare Parthian 𐫃𐫗𐫅𐫇𐫖 (gndwm /⁠gandum⁠/), Sogdian 𐼲𐼻𐽂𐼺 (γntm /⁠γandam⁠/), Northern Luri گںنم (gənem), Northern Kurdish genim, Pashto غنم (ǧanëm), Talysh گندم (qandım), Ave
Inherited from Middle Persian [Term?] (/⁠gandanāk⁠/), suffixing the word behind گند (stench) also found in گندلاش (gandalâš).
From Middle Persian [script needed] (gndk' /⁠gandag⁠/, “foul, stinking”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *g(ʰ)andʰ- (“to smell”); see Sanskrit गन्ध (gandhá) for more.

Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gwng /⁠gung⁠/), [Book Pahlavi needed] (gng /⁠gung⁠/, “dumb, mute”). Perhaps developed from the sense "to mock, hum", usually connected to Sanskrit गुञ्जति (guñjati, “buzz, hum”), itself of imitative origin. Compare also Proto-New Indo-Aryan *गुङ्ग

From Middle Persian [script needed] (gwh /⁠gūh⁠/), perhaps ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *g(ʷ)uH-. Cognate with Northern Kurdish gû, Northern Luri گی (gi), Proto-Slavic *govьno and Sanskrit गूथ (gūtha).
From Middle Persian gʾswʾlk' (gāhwārag, “cot, cradle”). Equivalent to گه (gah) + ـواره (-vâre), compare Northern Luri گواراْ (goāra).
Already Middle Persian, whence Arabic جَوَارِش (jawāriš), equivalent to گواشتن (govâštan) + ـش (-eš).

From Middle Persian [Term?], ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʷṓws + *h₂eǵ-. Cognate with Avestan 𐬔𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬁𐬰𐬀 (gauuāza, “ox-goad”), Sanskrit गवजन (gavájana, “whip, stick for driving cattle”) and Old Armenian գաւազան (gawazan) (a loanword).
From Middle Persian gwkl'-tn' (gugārīdan), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *wí (“apart”) + *kʷer- (“to do, make, construct”); literally meaning “to do away”.

From Middle Persian gwk’dy (gugāy). From Proto-Indo-European *wí (“apart”) + *kʷeḱ- (“to see”); literally meaning “to see apart, differentiate”. Compare Old Armenian վկայ (vkay), an Iranian borrowing.
From Middle Persian gwtl (*gōdar, “calf”).
Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gpl /⁠gabr⁠/), [script needed] (gwbl /⁠gabr⁠/, “hollow, cavity, womb”). Akin to Manichaean Middle Persian [script needed] (gbr /⁠gabr⁠/).
From Middle Persian gwl (gōr, “onager, wild ass”).
From گور (gōr, “zebra”) + خر (xar, “donkey”), both components being inherited from Middle Persian, see them for more.

Inherited from Middle Persian 𐭢𐭥𐭦 (gōz, “walnut”), from unattested Old Persian *angauza, probably ultimately from Old Iranian, with the preverb *han-, from Proto-Iranian *gauz- (“to hide, conceal”) (compare Sanskrit गूहति (gū́hati, “to cover, conceal”)), referring to the fact that the edible nut is

From Middle Persian KYNA (gōspand, “sheep, small cattle”), from Avestan 𐬔𐬀𐬊-𐬯𐬞𐬆𐬧𐬙𐬀- (gao-spəṇta-, “beneficent cow”), a compound of 𐬔𐬀𐬊- (gao-, “cow”) + 𐬯𐬞𐬆𐬧𐬙𐬀 (spəṇta, “holy”), compare گاو (gāw /gâv) and سپند (sipand /sepand).

Inherited from Middle Persian 𐭢𐭥𐭱 (gʿš /⁠gōš⁠/), from Old Persian 𐎥𐎢𐏁 (g-u-š /⁠gauša⁠/, “ear”), from Proto-Iranian *gáwšah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *gʰáwšas, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰows- (“hear”). Indo-Iranian cognates include: Avestan 𐬔𐬀𐬊𐬱𐬀 (gaoša), Baluchi گوش (goš), Northern Kurdish guh, Osse
Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gwšt' /⁠gōšt⁠/, “meat, flesh”), from Proto-Iranian *gawštaH. See it for more.

From Middle Persian [script needed] (gwšk' /⁠gōšag⁠/, “corner”), which appears to be a suffixed formation from the word found now as گوش (gōš, “ear”), in the sense of a lappet or protruding end of something.

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gwn' /⁠gōn⁠/, “colour, complexion”), from Proto-Iranian *gauna (“hair; color”), perhaps related to Sanskrit गुण (guṇa, “thread, cord”), with further origin beyond Indo-Iranian uncertain. Possibly from the BMAC substrate. Alternatively, from Proto-Indo-Europ
Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gwnk') (Manichaean script: 𐫃𐫇𐫗𐫃 (gwng /⁠gōnag⁠/, “sort, kind, form”)). Compare Iranian borrowing Old Armenian գունակ (gunak).
Inherited from Middle Persian gwhl (/⁠gōhr, gōhar⁠/, “substance, essence; jewel”). See there for more.

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gwklt'), 𐫃𐫇𐫃𐫏𐫡𐫅 (gwgyrd /⁠gōgird⁠/, “sulphur”), from Proto-Iranian *gawkr̥tah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *gawkr̥tas. Cognate with Sogdian 𐫄𐫇𐫐𐫤 (ɣwkt /⁠γōkət⁠/), Kamkata-viri geřtë.

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gwd /⁠gōy⁠/, “ball”). Cognate with Sanskrit गोल (gola), Persian گلوله (golule, “pellet; bullet”), Northern Luri گولٛاْ (goła, “pellet”), Central Kurdish گولە (gule) and گۆ (go, “ball”), Northern Kurdish gog (“ball”), Zazaki gudi (“ball; round”) and an Irani

Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gc /⁠gač⁠/, “plaster, gypsum”), ultimately from Akkadian 𒅎𒌓 (IM.BABBAR /⁠gaṣṣu⁠/, “gypsum”). Compare Khotanese [script needed] (gatsä, “gypsum”), Arabic جَصّ (jaṣṣ, “plaster”), Classical Syriac ܓܨܐ (gaṣṣā, “plaster”) from the same source.
From attested Middle Persian [script needed] (wiyāxan), from Proto-Iranian *wiyāxana, thus probably related to Avestan 𐬬𐬌𐬌𐬁𐬑𐬥𐬀 (viiāxna), 𐬬𐬌𐬌𐬁𐬑𐬀𐬥𐬀 (viiāxana) 'eloquent, orator'.

Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (wyʾn /⁠wiyān⁠/, “tent”), from Proto-Iranian *widaHna- (“tent”). Compare Parthian 𐫇𐫅𐫀𐫗 (wdʾn /⁠wiδān⁠/), Baluchi گدان (gedán), Old Armenian loanword վրան (vran).

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gyʾh /⁠giyāh⁠/, “grass”), from a compound formation related to Avestan 𐬔𐬀𐬊𐬛𐬁𐬌𐬌𐬎 (gaodāiiu, “grass”, literally “cow-giver”), or that which nourishes the cow, synchronically analyzable as گاو (gâv, “cow”) + دادَن (dâdan, “to give”). Compare with Manichaean Mi
From Middle Persian gytyḵ (gētīg, “the material world; worldly”).
From Middle Persian [script needed] (gytyk /⁠gēdīg⁠/) (attested in Husraw ī Kawādān ud rēdag-ē), probably from Sanskrit केतक (ketaka).

From Middle Persian gys (gēs, “curl, locks”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *káyćas ~ *gáyćas, of unknown source, likely a borrowing from the the BMAC substrate. Compare Manichaean Middle Persian gyswg (gēsūg). Akin to Old Armenian գէս (gēs), an Iranian borrowing. Cognate with Avestan 𐬔𐬀𐬉𐬯𐬎 (gaēsu, “curls
Inherited from Middle Persian 𐭠𐭩𐭥𐭯 (ʾywp /⁠ayāb⁠/) / 𐫀𐫏𐫀𐫁 (ʾyʾb /⁠ayāb⁠/). Cognate with Parthian 𐫀𐫃𐫀𐫖 (ʾgʾm /⁠āgām⁠/). Further etymology unclear; not found in Old Persian.

From Middle Persian [Term?] (/⁠ayād⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *Habí- + *yáH- (probably from Proto-Indo-European *yeh₂- (“to go; to go in, to enter”), with Iranian semantic shift "to enter [the mind]" > "to remember"). Compare Tocharian A [Term?] (opyāc, “in remembrance”), probably borrowed from an East
Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] ('byd'tk'l /⁠ayādgār⁠/, “memoir, testament”). By surface analysis, یاد (yād /yâd, “memory”) + گار (gār /gâr).
From Middle Persian 𐫏𐫀𐫉𐫅𐫍 (yʾzdh), [Book Pahlavi needed] (yʾcdẖ /⁠yāzdah⁠/), from earlier *yvāzdah, from Old Persian *aivacadaθa.

From Middle Persian 𐭩𐭠𐭮𐭬𐭭𐭠 (yʾsmn' /⁠yāsaman⁠/, “jasmine”). Akin to Sogdian 𐫝𐫀𐫢𐫖𐫗 (cʾšmn /⁠jāsmin⁠/) and the Iranian borrowings: Classical Syriac ܝܣܡܐ (yasmā), Jewish Babylonian Aramaic יסמין (/⁠ysmyn⁠/), Byzantine Greek ἰάσμη (iásmē), Old Armenian յասմիկ (yasmik).

From Middle Persian [script needed] (’y’ptn' /⁠ayāftan⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *Habí + *Hap- (“to reach, attain”). The prefix is from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Habʰí (“to, against, for”), while the root is from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ep- (“to take, seize, grab”). Cognate with Talysh آبه (ābe).
Inherited from Middle Persian yʾknd (yākand), from Ancient Greek ὑάκινθος (huákinthos). Doublet of یاقوت (yāqūt).
From Middle Persian yẕdʾn' (yazdān, “gods, spirits”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *yeh₁ǵ- (“to revere, worship, sacrifice”).

parole.significato: yasht (any of a collection of hymns and prayers)
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Persian yšt' (yašt, “prayer, worship”), probably from Avestan 𐬫𐬀𐬱𐬙𐬀 (yašta, “honored”).

parole.significato: to worship, to perform Zoroastrian rituals
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (yštn' /⁠yaštan⁠/), borrowed from Avestan 𐬫𐬀𐬰𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬌 (yazaⁱti, “to worship, to venerate”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hyáȷ́ati, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁yaǵ-.

Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (yl /⁠yal⁠/, “hero”), of unclear further etymology. Initial ya- cannot be directly inherited from Proto-Iranian. It is possibly a borrowing from Alanic or some other Northeastern Iranian descendant of Proto-Iranian *Áryah (“Aryan, Iranian”), whence
From Middle Persian ywc (yōz); see there for further information.

From earlier جغ (joġ), from Middle Persian ywg (juğ, “yoke”), from Proto-Iranian *yugám, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *yugám, from Proto-Indo-European *yugóm. From the same root are جفت (joft) and, via Greek and Arabic, زُوج (zowj), both meaning “pair, couple; partner; even number”. Cognate with English

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (ʾywk' /⁠yak⁠/), 𐫏𐫐 (yk /⁠yak⁠/), from Middle Persian: [Book Pahlavi needed] (ʾy /⁠ē⁠/), 𐭧𐭣 (HD), 𐫙𐫏𐫇 (ʿyw /⁠ēw⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *Háywah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Háywas, from Proto-Indo-European *óywos. Indo-European cognates include Bactrian ιωγο, Sa
Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (ʾywkʾnk' /⁠ēkānag⁠/). By surface analysis, یک (yak /yek, “one”) + ـانه (-āna /-âne).
